messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx spike detected on prod api-redwood-gateway. 5xx-rate > 3% over the last 5m. Paging oncall: @Alice. Autoscale attempted, some upstream errors returned 502/503. Correlation-id sample: corr=rhx-7a2f

Alice: oncall here. I see the alert. Can folks paste quick customer impact numbers and any obvious recent deploys? :eyes:

Dan: Support seeing a spike of error reports, ~12 customers reporting degraded generation results since ~22:06UTC. Not a full outage but high error surface area, some embeddings also affected.

Bob: I pulled the gateway logs. Lots of upstream 503 from runtime-pool-3. Looks like retries are hammering upstream and amplifying. Sample log (filtered):

```
[2026-03-14T22:06:58Z] request_id=rhx-7a2f method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=status=503 upstream_id=runtime-pool-3 latency=123ms retry=1
[2026-03-14T22:07:01Z] request_id=rhx-8b3c method=POST path=/v1/chat status=503 upstream=status=503 upstream_id=runtime-pool-3 latency=34ms retry=2
```

Bob: grep commands I ran:
```
# find related traces
rg "runtime-pool-3" /var/log/gateway/*.log | head
# correlation probe
jq -r '.headers["x-correlation-id"]' requests.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
```

Alice: No deploys in the last hour from product. Carmen any changes to runtime or autoscale?

Carmen: Nothing deployed. We rolled a kernel optimization two days ago but stable since. Autoscaler did spin up nodes but health checks show two runtimes flapping (runtime-3a, runtime-3b). My theory: a memory pressure or a bad model instance causing OOM-like crashes -> upstream 503s -> gateway retries amplify load.

Alice: Good hypothesis. Can we get a flame or some mem stats from the nodes? Also, wrap access to the model backend with a short-circuit so we don't keep retrying the same failing host.

Bob: Pulling node metrics now. Top lines:
```
# kubectl -n runtime top pod | egrep "runtime-3"
runtime-3a    950m (cpu)   12Gi (mem)  <unhealthy>
runtime-3b    980m         13Gi       <unhealthy>
```

Bob: Runtime logs show repeated kernel allocations failing, followed by process exit + kubelet restart. Example stack snippet:
```
E OOM killer invoked: oom_score_adj=0, process=model-server pid=2345
I SIGKILL sent
```

Dan: Customer impact: top 10 affected orgs show ~3-8% of their requests failing during the spike window. One enterprise partner (OrgID: org-77) reported 45 failed calls in a 20m window, mainly inference POSTs.

Ellen: Do we have a short public-facing note ready for status page? We should say degraded generation with elevated 5xx and we're investigating. Frank, can you coordinate customer comms for OrgID org-77 and a sync for any high-visibility customers?

Frank: On it. Sending targeted messages now. Will include corr ids (rhx-7a2f, rhx-8b3c) so they can surface logs on their side.

Carmen: Quick mitigation options: (1) cordon and drain runtime-3a/3b to stop flapping instances, (2) disable autoscale burst to avoid spinning up similar instances, (3) toggle gateway retry policy to 0 for 503s to stop amplification.

Alice: Do (3) first - disable retries to avoid amplification. Then drain the two pods. Bob, can you flip retry header on the gateway route?

Bob: Doing it now. Patch:
```
# gateway config snippet
routes:
  - name: generate
    upstream_retries: 0   # changed from 2
```
Applied at 22:12UTC. Observing traffic. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alice: Noted. After retries off we should see lower upstream load. Carmen start cordon/drain when Bob confirms stabilization.

Bob: Traffic after change: 5xx-rate dropped from 3.4% -> 0.9% over 2m. Upstream error counts for runtime-pool-3 dropping. :thumbsup:

Carmen: Starting cordon/drain for runtime-3a/3b. Will replace with fresh nodes from the stable pool.

Bob: While draining, I'm also toggling a temporary fallback route to a different model variant (less memory-hungry) for high-memory requests. Config:
```
route-override: if request.flags.memory_hungry then upstream=model-compact else upstream=model-default
```
Applied 22:16UTC.

Dan: Support reporting errors are decreasing. Customer reports for OrgID org-77 now down from 45 -> 3 failed calls in last 10m.

Alice: Good. Let's build in-thread timeline and hypotheses for the RCA:
- timeline-22:06: alert fires (5xx spike)
- 22:07: oncall paged, initial logs show runtime-pool-3 503s
- 22:08: autoscale tried, created new pods but two pods flapped (runtime-3a/3b)
- 22:12: gateway retries disabled -> immediate reduction in amplified errors
- 22:14: cordon/drain of flapping pods started
- 22:16: fallback route to compact model enabled
- 22:20: error rate returned to baseline (~0.2%)

Hypotheses:
H1: OOM in model-server on runtime-3 nodes causing crashes -> upstream 503s -> amplified by gateway retries.
H2: A bad model version or memory leak in kernel optimizations leading to increased memory pressure.
H3: Transient underlying hardware/network hiccup causing retries to repeatedly hit same failing hosts (less likely given OOM logs).

Carmen: For RCA next steps I propose: collect kubelet OOM logs, core dumps from model-server, model version hashes on affected pods, and recent kernel/kernel module versions. I'll open a ticket with SRE-runbooks to attach artifacts.

Bob: Save related correlation ids for trace join: rhx-7a2f, rhx-8b3c, rhx-9d4e. I'll export full request traces and attach to the incident ticket.

Alice: Assignments: Carmen -> collect node core dumps + model hash. Bob -> full trace export + gateway config diff. Dan/Frank -> customer comms summary. Ellen -> draft status page update. I'll own the incident timeline and handoff to next oncall if needed.

Ellen: Draft for status page (short):
"We are investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting text generation. We have implemented mitigations (disabled retry amplification and drained flapping runtime nodes). We will provide an update with root cause analysis."

Frank: Sent targeted notes to affected customers with correlation ids and ETA for follow-up.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated: 5xx-rate returned to baseline at 22:20UTC. Monitoring will watch for 30m. Incident severity lowered to SEV2.

Alice: Marking this thread as the live coordination log. We'll convert to a formal postmortem with the artifacts Carmen/Bob collect. If nothing else, handoff at 23:00UTC to @Bob for overnight monitoring.

Bob: Ack. I'll keep an eye and follow up with trace artifacts.

Carmen: Uploading core dumps + pod specs to the ticket now. Will include model version: model-v2.14-optim.

Dan: Closing support incident numbers in our tracker and noting impacted sessions per org.

Alice: Thanks all. Quick reminder for RCA: verify if model-v2.14-optim introduced memory regression (compare mem profiles v2.13 vs v2.14), and consider adding a memory guard to model-server to fail fast rather than hang.

Bob: Adding that to the action items. We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth and add attachments to the incident ticket.

Ellen: I'll schedule a postmortem runbook review after preliminary RCA is ready.

Frank: Closing customer follow-ups for now. Will reopen if they see recurrence.

Alice: End of live mitigation. Keeping incident open for RCA artifacts until tomorrow EOD.
